clusters.title: An unsent dispatch draft (location and text) is wiped when the Lightkeeper visits Map, Notebook or Circle and comes back to Roster.

clusters.title: The assignment's Illumination tally can be added twice from a second tab or another device, because its 'added' state and question ticks live only in one browser's localStorage.

A fresh browser after the Add also shows a live button. The dm seat saw the question ticks send no WebSocket message (illumTallies persisted in gameStore.js ~1608/2144), so other devices never see them. The circle can advance early, the harm the first report described.
clusters.expected: Once an assignment's tally is added, every Lightkeeper desk shows 'Added N Illumination'; the ticks and the added flag are stored on the circle.

clusters.steps: 1. Open reports, one player files a report with a key. 2. Lightkeeper opens Circle page in tab A, then tab B. 3. In B tick a question and press Add N Illumination. 4. Back in A press 'Use this tab', press Add again. 5. Or open the desk in a fresh browser after the Add.
clusters.notes: Fix that brought a new problem (regress verdict fixed-but-new-problem). Wrong Illumination number and early advancement, so high.

clusters.title: On a phone the creator's path card arrows sit below the fold, under the sticky bottom bar, and nothing says there are ten paths or that the card can be swiped.
clusters.summary: Phone 390x844 and 390x705, step 1 Choose Path: the first view shows only the Journalist card and a disabled 'Select this path'; the Previous/Next arrows are under the tall card, covered by the sticky footer. Nine 'Next card' taps left it on 1/10; after scrolling about 450 px the arrows worked. Seen at character creation and again when building the replacement investigator.
clusters.expected: Arrows visible on first view (or beside the card), or a hint such as '1 of 10, swipe'.
clusters.actual: Arrows off screen under the footer; no hint of the other nine paths.
clusters.steps: 1. Phone 390x844, New investigator. 2. Without scrolling look for a way to the next path. 3. Scroll down and use Next card.
clusters.notes: Harness artifact in the 'taps did nothing' part: seat.js --tap sends a raw CDP touch at the element's centre after scrollIntoViewIfNeeded with no check that it is covered, so the taps landed on the sticky footer. A horizontal swipe on the card does turn it (CharacterCreator.jsx:651), and the stacked card edges hint at more cards, so this is a discoverability nit. Related to the first report's path-cards-tablet-navigation (fixed for the tablet).

clusters.title: Pass Notes still offers the sender as a recipient, has no Lightkeeper-only choice, and never says the Lightkeeper reads private notes, so a player cannot reply privately to the Lightkeeper.

clusters.title: Illumination milestones are still explained by nothing a touch screen can reach, and the milestone log line says nothing of what it gives.

clusters.title: A circle-question vote was recorded on the tablet that the player says they never cast.
clusters.summary: Tablet 820x1180: on opening the desk with the formation papers up, Dev tapped the Circle tab; question I then showed 'your vote'. dev.events.jsonl shows circle_creation_vote question q1 sent at 03:42:47, six seconds after ws_open and before any other vote.

clusters.title: The gilded keep-one-die choice keeps wobbling, so automated clicks and taps time out and needed force.
clusters.summary: Desktop 1920x1080 (Ada, about seven rolls), laptop 1366x768 (Cass) and tablet 820x1180 (Dev): Playwright reports 'element is not stable' on the keep-die choice and times out; a forced click (or, once on the tablet, a dispatched click) kept the die. The candidate dice run animate-liftShimmy (1.5 s, infinite; DiceTray.jsx:178, index.css:186-195). Ada and Dev named it the thing that got in their way most.
clusters.expected: A still, unambiguous target for the most important choice of a gilded roll.
clusters.actual: The target moves continuously; automation needs force.
clusters.steps: 1. Roll a gilded action. 2. Click or tap a keep-die choice without force.
clusters.notes: Known harness quirk ('the gilded keep die wobbles, so automation needs force or Enter'). prefers-reduced-motion is honoured (index.css:1190 caps every animation to one 0.01 ms iteration), and a real pointer can hit an 8 px wobble, so the human impact is small. Dev's wrong keep (F214) came from seat.js substring matching ('Keep the 4' vs 'Keep the gilded 4'). F177/F206 also report the full-drive refund wording, clustered separately.

clusters.title: The gilded keep choice promises '1 <drive> back' and the log says '1 refreshed' when the drive is already full and nothing comes back.

clusters.steps: 1. Drive at its maximum. 2. Roll a gilded action. 3. Read the keep choices; keep the gilded die; read the log and drive.
clusters.notes: A wording problem the gilded-choice-unexplained fix brought; the cap itself is correct.

clusters.title: The Lightkeeper's trauma Edit cannot add a scar, so a story-given scar needs a full four-mark cycle, and removing a killing scar leaves its action shift behind.

clusters.title: The 'Burn and reroll' offer disappears without a word as soon as anyone else at the table rolls, and the dice button's 'choice waiting' dot does not match it.

clusters.title: The client and the server disagree on when a roll is settled: the Lightkeeper's roll does not settle a player's burn on the server, and a gilded die kept after another roll loses its Burn offer while the server still takes the burn.

DiceVault's settled test checks only that some tableRoll exists.

clusters.actual: Stale burn accepted in one case, burn hidden but accepted in the other.
clusters.steps: See the regress evidence: case 1 drops a phone's socket during the Lightkeeper's open roll; case 2 has another player roll while a gilded keep waits.
clusters.notes: Fix brought these narrow timing cases; regress reproduced both in the browser.

clusters.title: Ally ability offers are lost on a reload though the server still takes them, and a second ally's card stays up for a mark already taken, then fails silently.

clusters.title: An old roll's Burn and reroll offer comes back after End Assignment and a Refresh, hours after the roll.

praise.title: The desk stays live without reloads
praise.summary: On every device (phone 390, tablet 820, laptops, desktop 1920) approvals, marks, scars, dispatches, notes, reports, advancement dialogs and a newcomer's welcome dialog arrived live; players and the Lightkeeper never reloaded all night. Named as 'keep exactly as is' by four seats. F190 notes the welcome dialog grabbed the screen mid-action and swallowed a tap.

praise.title: The server restart was invisible to the table
praise.summary: Across the 04:15:29 to 04:15:59 restart every desk (laptop, phone, tablet, desktop) reconnected by itself, with no leftover banner, nothing lost, and later events arriving live.

praise.title: Sign-up and account flows work end to end
praise.summary: Fresh-database sign-up works first time (confirms the first report's 500-on-first-account fix); forgot-password works on a phone with the username prefilled; email change runs form to confirm page cleanly.

praise.title: The reworked creator is clear on every screen
praise.summary: Four locked steps, live counters, limits announced to screen readers, clear presets and join status at once; good on desktop, phone and tablet.

praise.title: Join requests and the Lightkeeper's formation view
praise.summary: View sheet before approving and requests keeping pronouns and catalyst after an approval (confirms first report #28 / join-requests-lose-details and the sheet-preview fix); Circle formation so far shows who has voted or answered (confirms lk-formation-status-thin); the hub shows Awaiting approval; a second campaign's code with stray spaces is accepted.

praise.title: Formation papers handle ties and edge cases
praise.summary: Ties are stated on screen with leading and your-vote markers; case and spacing duplicate names are refused with a pointer (confirms name-case-duplicates); seal kept the leading name in a 2-2 tie (confirms vote-tie-leading); counter form offers the relationship's questions; the dispatch template picks up the renamed circle.

praise.title: Dispatch, timer and secret roll behave and log as a Lightkeeper expects
praise.summary: Timer events reach the log and the screen-reader status clears with the timer (confirms first report #7 and #42); dispatches, locations and tension names each get a log line; secret rolls and private notes stay private.

praise.title: Rolls and pools are right and clear
praise.summary: Phone roll flow with drive spend and gilded refund is clear; Open Book pools match the FAQ; keyboard-only play works with a visible focus ring and announced results.

praise.title: Double presses do exactly one thing
praise.summary: Double-click and Enter-twice on keep-die, Pass Notes, Send report, votes and circle resource spends each did one thing (confirms first report report-forgets-sent and resource-double-click-double-spend fixes).

praise.title: Scars, death and its take-back are handled with care
praise.summary: Scar forms work on a phone and update the sheet at once; the fourth scar warns, shows a clear death dialog and a live Deceased section; removing the killing scar is warned and logged; the Lightkeeper's one-click Deal a mark is a keeper.

praise.title: Assignment reports and the Illumination tally match the book
praise.summary: Send locks the boxes with a REPORT SENT stamp and Amend (confirms report-forgets-sent); the next assignment's form starts empty; the tally follows p. 55, counts the newcomer and not the dead, and adds once (confirms report-questions-tally).

praise.title: Advancement and End Assignment wrap up cleanly
praise.summary: Track full offers a clear advancement dialog that arrives live on every device, Later leaves a way back, picks grey out at the limit; End Assignment says what stays and resets spends, reports closed 0 of 4 (confirms end-assignment-reports-open).

praise.title: Circle resource spends are safe and live
praise.summary: Two-tap confirm, counts and drives update live, a third spend is refused with a reason.

praise.title: The Notebook feels like a real field journal
praise.summary: Markdown preview, photographs and the sketch tool work first try on a tablet and kept all five entries through a restart, a death and two assignment closes.

praise.title: Invite and Save and rejoin turn a death into a new start
praise.summary: The invite banner follows the player into the creator, Save and rejoin is one tap, and the table gets a welcome dialog with the relationship form.

praise.title: A second campaign is easy to start and leaves the first intact
praise.summary: One small form; the Case Ledger lists both; returning to the first desk finds it current.
